# Findings and back-test (generated by scripts/analyse.py)

Data: 2018 rows -> 1987 usable COD orders, 01 Apr to 30 Sep 2026. Overall RTO rate 28.4%.
Model trained on Apr-Aug (1658 orders), tested on September (329 orders) which it never saw.

## Data quality (fixed before anything else)

| Issue | Rows |
|---|---|
| Exact duplicate rows (same order ID, every field identical) | 30 |
| Status label variants ('Rto', 'delivered', 'RTO ') | 4 |
| Order still IN_TRANSIT (no outcome, dropped) | 1 |
| Phone in +91 format (normalised) | 15 |
| Phone only 9 digits (invalid) | 17 |
| Pincode missing | 12 |
| Order value ₹0 | 3 |
| Prior RTOs greater than prior orders (capped) | 4 |


## Findings

**1. Pincode history is too thin to act on.** 1066 distinct pincodes; 554 of them have exactly one order, and only 161 orders (8%) sit in pincodes with 5+ orders. The signal lives one level up, in the pincode district (first 3 digits):

| District | City | Orders | RTO rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 273xxx | Gorakhpur | 44 | 64% |
| 846xxx | Darbhanga | 61 | 61% |
| 243xxx | Bareilly | 33 | 61% |
| 470xxx | Sagar | 53 | 49% |
| 800xxx | Patna | 80 | 48% |
| 324xxx | Kota | 39 | 41% |
| 781xxx | Guwahati | 42 | 36% |
| 226xxx | Lucknow | 117 | 32% |
| 452xxx | Indore | 72 | 31% |
| 302xxx | Jaipur | 120 | 27% |
| 500xxx | Hyderabad | 172 | 26% |
| 560xxx | Bengaluru | 212 | 25% |
| 700xxx | Kolkata | 127 | 23% |
| 110xxx | Delhi | 240 | 22% |
| 600xxx | Chennai | 152 | 21% |
| 400xxx | Mumbai | 218 | 18% |
| 411xxx | Pune | 169 | 18% |

**2. Bad addresses are the strongest single signal - but even they mostly aren't fraud.**
| Address | Orders | RTO rate | Delivered anyway |
|---|---|---|---|
| complete | 1323 | 23% | 77% |
| landmark_only | 481 | 31% | 69% |
| unusable | 183 | 62% | 38% |

Hinglish/landmark addresses ('ph krke aana, Govt School ke paas') return at 31% - close to average, so they must not be penalised as 'bad'. Fake-looking names (44 orders) return at 64%, but the 8 with a proper address returned at 0%: the address does the work, the name barely matters.

**3. Past behaviour beats everything else.**
| Customer | Orders | RTO rate |
|---|---|---|
| repeat, never refused | 350 | 14% |
| first order | 1495 | 30% |
| repeat, refused once | 112 | 38% |
| repeat, refused 2+ | 30 | 73% |

**4. Big COD baskets come back more:** 39% RTO at ₹1,500+ (281 orders) vs 27% below.

**5. Meta ads bring the riskiest first orders:** first-time buyers from Meta ads RTO at 34% vs 22% for direct traffic (all Meta orders: 31%, n=765).

**6. Courier matters less than it looks** - outside the four high-RTO states: Delhivery 20%, BlueDart 24%, Shadowfax 24%, Xpressbees 25%, Ecom Express 25%.


## Unit economics (from the brief)

- One RTO costs **₹169**: ₹65 out + ₹65 back + ₹25 handling + 8% × ₹180 damaged stock.
- One delivered ₹649 order earns **₹337** (62% margin - ₹65 shipping), **₹412** for a first-time buyer once their likely future orders are counted.
- So cancelling only pays when an order is more likely to fail than succeed by a wide margin: break-even risk = 67% (repeat) / 71% (first-time). The average COD order is at 28%.
- Future value of a first-time buyer: repeat orders are 492 of 1987 (25%), i.e. ~0.33 repeat orders per new buyer in steady state; × ~₹230 expected contribution per repeat order ≈ ₹75. The ₹300 Meta CAC is already spent when we decide, so it does not enter the per-order maths - what a cancellation destroys is this order's margin plus that future value.

## How big should the prepaid discount be?

Moving one COD buyer with risk p to prepaid is worth (p_conv − 4%) × (delivered value + RTO cost), where p_conv = 0.5 × p because people who accept are less risky than their band. That is the most a discount can be before it loses money on every conversion:

| Order risk | Max discount that still pays (₹649 first-time order) |
|---|---|
| 15% | ₹20 |
| 25% | ₹49 |
| 35% | ₹79 |
| 50% | ₹122 |

We offer a flat **₹40** (~6% of AOV): it pays for itself from ~25% risk upward, which is where the nudge band starts. Below that, a discount mostly goes to people who would have paid anyway. Flat ₹ rather than % because it reads clearly in a WhatsApp message and caps the cost on big baskets.

## Choosing the thresholds

Grid search over nudge/confirm/hold thresholds on Apr-Aug orders (using real outcomes): best was nudge from 20%, confirm from 60%, hold from 70% (net ₹9,438 over 5 months). The config ships with nudge 25 / confirm 50 / hold 75.

The grid winner is tuned to assumptions we haven't measured yet, so we also check each candidate when WhatsApp confirmation works worse than assumed (catches 25% of RTOs, loses 15% of genuine buyers):

| Nudge / confirm / hold from (%) | Net Apr-Aug | Net Sept | Net Sept, weak confirmation | Sept nudge / confirm / hold orders |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 / 60 / 70 | ₹9,438 | ₹2,840 | ₹1,661 | 156 / 33 / 9 |
| 25 / 35 / 75 | ₹5,801 | ₹2,336 | -₹700 | 61 / 79 / 9 |
| 25 / 40 / 75 | ₹7,442 | ₹2,600 | ₹279 | 79 / 61 / 9 |
| 25 / 50 / 75 **(chosen)** | ₹8,877 | ₹3,093 | ₹1,737 | 99 / 41 / 9 |
| 20 / 50 / 75 | ₹8,929 | ₹2,897 | ₹1,540 | 148 / 41 / 9 |


## What each approach would have done to September (329 COD orders)

| Approach | Actions | RTO cost saved | Genuine margin lost | Discounts + WhatsApp | Net vs today |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ship everything (today) | 0 held | ₹0 | ₹0 | ₹0 | ₹0 |
| Ops: cancel if risk ≥40% or area >45% RTO (4 districts) | 71 cancelled | ₹7,486 | ₹16,562 | ₹354 | -₹9,431 |
| Recommended rules | 9 held, 41 confirm, 99 nudge | ₹5,344 | ₹1,499 | ₹752 | ₹3,093 |
| Recommended, but score may cancel first-timers | 10 held | ₹5,452 | ₹1,499 | ₹754 | ₹3,199 |
| Per-order ₹ optimum (reference) | 6 held, 93 confirm, 88 nudge | ₹5,907 | ₹1,806 | ₹729 | ₹3,372 |

Scaled to a full month of COD (~1,650 orders, ×5.0): recommended ≈ **₹15,512/month**, Ops rule ≈ **-₹47,298/month**.

Recommended buckets in September: ship: 180 orders (11% actually RTO'd), nudge: 99 orders (37% actually RTO'd), confirm: 41 orders (51% actually RTO'd), hold: 9 orders (89% actually RTO'd).

Rule hits in September: fake-looking name AND unusable address (6), possible double order (4), customer refused 2 earlier COD orders (3), address too vague (3), phone number invalid (2), first-time buyer (1).

## How sure are we? (sensitivity of the recommended rules, September)

Confirmation and nudge results are assumptions until measured. Net ₹ for September under other values:

| Scenario | Net, September sample | Net per month (scaled) |
|---|---|---|
| Base case | ₹3,093 | ₹15,512 |
| Confirmation catches only 25% of RTOs | ₹2,381 | ₹11,941 |
| Confirmation loses 15% of genuine buyers | ₹2,448 | ₹12,277 |
| Both of the above | ₹1,737 | ₹8,711 |
| Only 5% take the prepaid offer | ₹2,264 | ₹11,354 |
| New buyer worth ₹300 more (Marketing's view) | ₹3,089 | ₹15,492 |
